title: People, Things and Places
subtitle: A practical revision pack for useful questions, clear descriptions, and office messages.

days.title: Day 1 — Ask and answer clearly
days.intro: Use some, any, and compound words in useful messages.

activities.title: Useful messages
activities.instructions: Read the examples and make one sentence about your day.
activities.content: Is there anyone who can help? There is something on the shelf. Nobody is in the room. Everything is ready.

activities.title: Ask about people and things
activities.content: Use anyone in a general question and no one when a place has no people.

questions.prompt: You need help with a visitor. What do you ask?
options: Is there anyone who can help?
Is there everyone who can help?
Is there nothing who can help?

questions.prompt: The meeting room is empty. Which message fits?
options: Everyone is in the meeting room.
No one is in the meeting room.
Anything is in the meeting room.

activities.title: Asking for help
activities.instructions: Read both roles and change the item in brackets.

dialogue.speaker: Mina
dialogue.text: Is there anyone who can help with this [parcel]?

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Yes. Someone from reception can help.

dialogue.speaker: Mina
dialogue.text: Is there anything else to prepare?

patterns: Is there anyone who can help?

days.title: Day 2 — Explain where things are
days.intro: Use there is and place phrases to guide a visitor.

activities.title: Give a visitor a clear route
activities.instructions: Read the route aloud, then describe one place near you.
activities.content: There is a notice opposite reception. The parcel is under the desk. The delivery room is below the office.

activities.title: A visitor arrives
activities.instructions: Read the message and choose the detail that answers each question.
activities.content: A visitor has an appointment at two. There is a notice opposite reception with her name. The meeting room is behind reception, and a parcel is under the desk.

activities.title: Office visit
activities.instructions: Read both roles aloud, then answer the questions.

dialogue.speaker: Guide
dialogue.text: There is a chair on the balcony if you want to wait.

dialogue.speaker: Guide
dialogue.text: It is behind reception, opposite the kitchen.

activities.title: Finding the room

dialogue.speaker: Visitor
dialogue.text: Is there a notice near reception?

patterns: Is there a notice near reception?

days.title: Day 3 — Write and say useful messages
days.intro: Use the new language in a practical office situation.

activities.title: Write a message for a visitor
activities.instructions: Write 4–6 sentences for a visitor with an appointment. Say where to wait, who can help, and where the meeting room is. This written work is for review.
activities.content: Useful starters: Is there anyone? There is… Nobody is… The room is behind…

activities.title: Explain an office visit
activities.instructions: Say four short sentences aloud. Include one person word, one thing word, and two place descriptions.

activities.title: Final check before a call
activities.instructions: Read both roles, then make the details your own.

dialogue.speaker: Lara
dialogue.text: Is everyone ready for the call?

dialogue.speaker: Lara
dialogue.text: Is there anything else to prepare?
